inputs.original_text: Daniel Rubenstein’s call for a political resolution is important, but it sits uneasily beside a message still organized around Israel’s “unwavering stance” and an ongoing operation. That is the problem with treating military pressure as the center of security: it can perpetuate the very conditions that keep people across the region unsafe. A durable resolution has to confront the structures behind the conflict and protect people’s rights, not make endless escalation sound like the only option.
inputs.modified_text: Rubenstein is right that a political resolution matters, but peace cannot rest on asking Israel to abandon a firm stance while an operation is ongoing. A government’s first duty is to protect its people and preserve order; treating security measures as the cause of the danger risks excusing those who threaten it. Rights matter, but so do public safety and the stability families need. Any lasting settlement has to take those responsibilities seriously, not make restraint by one side the whole plan.
